ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, and authorized signatories against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and sectoral regulations); (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) Luxembourg Ministry of Finance asset-freeze notifications; and (iv) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list as market practice for USD SWIFT clearing. PEP status is screened under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02; enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth evidence, and senior-management approval are mandatory for any higher-risk PEP.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal (www.lbr.lu), operated by the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registration language is French. The corporate name must be expressed in Latin-script characters; where a Chinese-character brand (e.g., Luosifen) is used, a romanized transliteration plus a registered French or English trade name is required. The name must include the mandatory suffix 'SCSp' or the full 'Société en commandite spéciale' and must not be contrary to public policy (bonnes moeurs).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Banquier, Crédit (CSSF prior authorization required)
Assurance, Assureur, Courtier d'assurance (CSSF/CAA prior authorization required)
Fonds de placement, OPC, OPCVM, SICAV, SICAF, FCP (CSSF prior registration required)
État, Gouvernement, Ministère, Commune, Nation (public-authority connotation prohibited)
Luxembourg or Luxembourgish derivatives used in a misleading public-institution context
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name clearance is requested electronically via the LBR platform before notarization. On approval, the name is reserved for 30 calendar days; a single 15-day extension may be requested in writing by counsel before expiry. If incorporation is not filed within the reservation window, the reservation lapses automatically. Upon rejection, counsel may file a written objection with the RCS within 15 days of the refusal notice. If the objection is unsuccessful, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Tribunal d'arrondissement (commercial chamber) within 30 days of the final refusal, failing which the refusal becomes final.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an SCSp used as a holding, financing, or investment platform: the SCSp must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg, which may be supplied by an RCS-approved domiciliation company via a virtual-office arrangement. A virtual office is NOT permissible where the SCSp itself conducts physical food manufacturing in Luxembourg; such manufacturing requires a licensed operational establishment and prior approval of the Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA) under Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 and national food-safety law. For the instant rice-noodle (Luosifen) project with production located outside Luxembourg, the SCSp's virtual or domiciled office is legally acceptable for its holding and trade-finance functions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% annual probability) for a disclosed non-operational SCSp holding vehicle without Luxembourg trading premises. Unannounced inspections would be triggered primarily by RBE disclosure anomalies, AML alerts, or notification of a Luxembourg food operation. If a Luxembourg ALVA food-establishment license were obtained, targeted on-site food-safety inspections would be mandatory at initial licensing and at least annually thereafter.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended — Articles 944-1 to 944-22 (Special Limited Partnership 'SCSp', inserted by the Law of 23 July 2016) and Article 4 (registration and publication requirements); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS); Law of 2 September 2011 on the freedom of establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 7 rue Espérance, L-1477 Luxembourg, www.lbr.lu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / contrat de société (partnership agreement) filed electronically via the RCS e-filing portal, with prior fixed registration duty paid to the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital and no escrow/paid-up requirement for an SCSp under Luxembourg law (Law of 10 August 1915, Art. 944-1). The partnership capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement; contributions may be in cash or in kind, may be staggered, and no bank escrow or capital deposit certificate is legally required for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER (GÉRANT): (1) The SCSp partnership agreement, presented to this meeting, is approved and adopted in final form; (2) The subscribers named in Schedule A are admitted as limited partners with the capital contributions set against their names, credited as made or promised pursuant to the agreement; (3) The registered office is fixed at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, with immediate effect; (4) [Name] is appointed sole Manager (Gérant) with full authority to open bank accounts, appoint counsel, and represent the partnership vis-à-vis third parties; and (5) The Manager is authorized to execute all statutory filings, registrations, and publications required for incorporation of the partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Verification and Partnership Agreement Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS database; authorized Luxembourg counsel or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the proposed corporate name against the RCS register to confirm the absence of identical or confusingly similar prior registrations and conformity with Luxembourg rules on corporate names. Engage counsel to draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société) under the Law of 10 August 1915 (Arts. 944-1 et seq.) in French or German, specifying legal form (SCSp), corporate name, registered office, corporate object (manufacture, retort canning and distribution of instant rice noodles, ISIC 1079), duration, capital, classes of partners, manager powers, and transfer rules.
required_dossiers: General partner's passport copy and proof of residence
Limited partners' passport copies and KYC/AML forms
Power of attorney to Luxembourg counsel or notary
Proposed corporate name and LBR/RCS name search confirmation
Draft partnership agreement (contrat de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name check identifies a conflicting or confusingly similar entity, select two alternative names and, if necessary, obtain a formal negative name certificate from the RCS; amend the draft deed accordingly before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Constitutive Deed and Payment of Fixed Registration Duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (for immovable contributions) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Registration Office (Bureau d'enregistrement), Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the partnership agreement by notarial deed where immovable property is contributed, or by private deed (acte sous seing privé) for cash or movable in-kind contributions. Obtain original signatures of all partners and the appointed Manager. Submit the executed deed to AEDT within 15 days of signature for fixed-duty registration (flat fee of EUR 25 for a non-immovable contribution; scaled duty for real estate). Retain the stamped AEDT receipt as proof.
required_dossiers: Original executed partnership agreement (minimum 3 counterparts)
Bank certificate or statement evidencing capital contribution or availability of funds
Identity documents and signature specimens of all partners
AEDT registration duty payment form or counsel's AEDT account debiting authorization
Notarial deed (if immovable property is contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late submission incurs a late-filing surcharge (taxe de retard) capped at EUR 75; the authorized agent may request remission (degrèvement gracieux) from AEDT by demonstrating first-time, good-faith non-compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RCS registration request electronically through the official LBR portal using the prescribed registration form. Attach the executed partnership agreement, declaration of acceptance of office by the Manager, criminal record extracts, identity documents, and AEDT proof of payment. State the legal form 'SCSp', registered office, corporate object (instant rice/noodle manufacturing and related food trade), duration and manager details. Pay the statutory RCS filing fee of EUR 19 online. The registrar performs legal control and allocates the RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (electronic copy)
Completed and signed RCS registration form
Declaration of acceptance of office by the Manager (Gérant)
Extract of criminal record (extrait du casier judiciaire) of the Manager and/or General Partner, issued within the last 3 months
AEDT receipt evidencing payment of registration duty
Power of attorney if filing is effected by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query or a project of refusal, remedy the indicated defect or file written observations within 15 days; an adverse final decision may be appealed to the District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the trade register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations — RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — RESA Publication Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, RCS automatically transmits a publication extract to RESA, the official electronic gazette. No separate partner action is required, but the General Partner must verify the online publication within 5 working days and confirm accuracy of the corporate name, RCS number, legal form, registered office, manager appointments, and object.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (certificat d'inscription)
RESA publication extract generated by the RCS
Internal verification checklist of published data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published entry is inaccurate, file a rectification request with the RCS together with the corrected excerpt and supporting evidence; corrections attributable to registrar error are processed free of charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations — Tax, VAT, Social Security and Business Establishment License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Direct Tax Administration); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (VAT Administration); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Ministry of the Economy — Direction générale des PME
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: RCS automatically transfers incorporation data to the Direct Tax Administration for allocation of the business registration number (matricule). The Manager must file VAT form 640 with the AEDT if taxable turnover exceeds the EUR 35,000 threshold, or voluntarily to secure input VAT recovery, indicating NACE code 1079. If the partnership employs staff, register with CCSS. For physical operation of a manufacturing establishment, apply to the Ministry of the Economy for the establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011, attaching the Manager's good character and professional qualification evidence, within 3 months of formation.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Executed partnership agreement
VAT registration form 640 (NACE code 1079)
Establishment authorization application file (Ministry of the Economy form)
Manager's professional qualifications and criminal record extract
CCSS employee registration forms (if hiring staff)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax matricule is not issued within 10 working days, follow up with the Direct Tax Administration and request RCS to re-transmit the e-filing data; refusal of the establishment authorization is appealable to the administrative courts within 3 months, and interim measures may be sought for low-risk preparatory works.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Direction générale des PME (Establishment Licensing) jointly with the Administration vétérinaire et de la sécurité alimentaire (ALVA — Luxembourg Veterinary and Food Administration) for food business approval under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and, where animal-origin ingredients are used, Regulation (EC) No 853/2004
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011, together with Food Business Operator Registration/Approval (enregistrement / agrément sanitaire) for the manufacture, retort thermal processing, and canning of instant rice noodles, including pressure equipment (retort autoclaves) conformity per Directive 2014/68/EU (PED)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified installation (établissement classé) under the Law of 24 July 2022 on environmental authorization and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 July 2022 on classifying installations; food manufacturing (prepared meals/canned noodles) with net annual production below 2,000 tonnes typically falls under Class 4 (declaration regime), requiring a compliance dossier without mandatory EIA; production of 2,000 tonnes or more per annum triggers Class 3 and a simplified environmental impact notice (notice d'impact); wastewater discharge authorization from the Administration de la gestion de l'eau is required under the Law of 19 December 2008 on water management.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits per Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 September 2019: COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L, pH 6–9, temperature ≤ 30°C; VOC emissions from cooking and cleaning processes limited to 20 mg C/Nm³ per EU Solvent Emissions Directive 1999/13/EC and Directive 2010/75/EU; solid food by-products and packaging waste managed per the waste hierarchy and traceability obligations of the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGIIS) covering fire alarms, extinguishers, evacuation routes and sprinkler verification; structural load inspection of production halls by an approved engineering bureau per the Law of 4 December 1967; occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) including workplace air quality, accident prevention, chemical agents, and periodic inspection/certification of retort autoclaves and pressure vessels under Directive 2014/68/EU and the Luxembourg Grand-Ducal Regulation on pressure equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: VAT registration and indirect tax compliance: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED), 1-3 avenue Guillaume, L-1651 Luxembourg. Income tax and partnerships: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), 43 boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg. Customs/excise and exports: Administration des douanes et accises (ADA), customs single window. Unified national e-portal: MyGuichet.lu (transactional e-filing for AED and ACD) and Guichet.lu; entity registration via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) e-platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SCSp partnership agreement by notarial deed and file for inscription with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through the LBR e-platform. Step 2: Upon registration the RCS/LBR attributes the national identification number (matricule) which functions as the statutory TIN for direct tax and annual accounts filings. Step 3: Submit VAT registration to the AED via Form 700 (MyGuichet.lu) specifying expected taxable turnover; the AED issues a distinct VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits). Registration is compulsory where the SCSp performs taxable supplies in Luxembourg above the EUR 35,000 small-enterprise threshold, or immediately for non-established persons, intra-EU acquisitions, and qualifying distance sales. Step 4: apply to the ADA for an EU EORI number before first physical export; the EORI is required for the export declaration. Step 5: the general partner must be designated as the SCSp's tax representative for ACD/AED formalities; non-resident partners need no separate Luxembourg tax representative merely by reason of holding LP interests.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The SCSp lacks legal personality and is fiscally transparent under Luxembourg direct tax law: income, gains, losses and net wealth are allocated pro rata to the partners and taxed at partner level (resident individuals: personal income tax; corporate partners: corporate income tax plus municipal business tax). The SCSp is nevertheless a separate taxable person for VAT, for customs/EORI purposes, and for excise/licensing formalities relating to food manufacture.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply U.S.-style check-the-box. Available elections and characterization mechanisms: (1) Article 185 LIR option for a qualifying commercial partnership to be taxed as a capital company (irrevocable, requires joint request to the ACD; results in entity-level CIT); (2) waiver of the small-enterprise VAT exemption under Article 57 of the VAT Act so as to obtain full input VAT deduction; (3) ATAD II hybrid-mismatch alignment under Articles 168b-168c LIR, allowing the SCSp and its foreign owners to apply consistent characterization (transparent vs opaque) where the counterpart jurisdiction taxes the SCSp as opaque; (4) OSS registration for intra-EU distance sales of packaged food (Articles 63bis-63quater VAT Act); and (5) Article 185-aligned cross-border rulings via the ACD advance ruling procedure confirming transparency for treaty purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the amended Law of 12 February 1979, harmonized with Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for established small businesses (Article 57 VAT Act small-enterprise exemption); zero-threshold registration obligation for non-established taxable persons and for intra-Community acquisitions; EUR 10,000 Union-wide threshold for intra-EU distance sales of goods governed by the One Stop Shop; food manufacturing engaged for commercial purposes is ordinarily registered from the first supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G electronic invoicing in the four-corner PEPPOL model under the Law of 27 November 2018 and implementing regulations for invoices issued to Luxembourg public contracting authorities after 1 March 2022; PEPPOL BIS 3.0 is the required format. No real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no AED pre-validation applies to B2B or B2C invoices; B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary and governed by private agreement. Export invoices must be readily referable to the customs export MRN in the AED audit context.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of instant rice noodle products physically leaving the European Union qualify for zero-rating with credit (exemption with right of deduction) under Article 56(1)(a) of the VAT Act provided: (i) property in the goods has transferred to a non-EU buyer; (ii) the goods are dispatched or transported out of the EU within the applicable documentary timeline; and (iii) the SCSp retains the full customs/transport evidence bundle. Intra-EU dispatches to a VAT-registered customer are exempt under Article 56(1)(c) with a valid EU VAT number. Offshore ancillary and logistics services supplied to non-EU counterparties are outside the Luxembourg VAT scope under place-of-supply rules or reverse-charged under Articles 58-60 VAT Act; freight services to third countries may be zero-rated under Article 56(1)(f).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (AES/ECS declaration released via the Luxembourg customs single window) with unique MRN and exit confirmation date
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR multimodal transport document evidencing dispatch to the non-EU destination and consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT credit notification from the foreign buyer evidencing cross-border payment and FX repatriation to the SCSp's Luxembourg bank account
Commercial invoice and packing list displaying full cross-reference to the MRN and transport document
Where goods are sold under EXW/FCA, a written export declaration from the buyer or authorization letter confirming the buyer's lodgement of the export customs declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED audits export zero-rating on the basis of documentary evidence existing at the time of assessment. Where the bundle is incomplete, inconsistent or unavailable, the supply is reclassified as a domestic Luxembourg sale and assessed at the standard VAT rate (16%) with statutory late-payment interest from the original due date. The normal assessment window is 3 years, extended to 5 years for established tax evasion; criminal fraud cases may run beyond 5 years. Administrative fines of EUR 250 to EUR 12,500 per infraction apply for non-registration, record-keeping, issuance and electron-proof deficiencies under the VAT Act. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims (falsified transport documents, sham intermediaries, premature/phoney exit declarations) expose the SCSp, its general partner and its directors to criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and custodial penalties under the Law of 12 February 1979, joint liability for the clawback VAT, possible loss of authorized-exporter and simplified declaration statuses, and debarment from future export facilitations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting with the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Eurosystem. Banking supervision and AML/CTF enforcement are exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro (EUR) is fully convertible. Luxembourg applies complete liberalization of capital and current account movements under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no prior approval requirements for inward or outward transfers within the EU/EEA. Profit remittances face no exchange control hurdle; practical frictions arise only from bank-level AML/KYC screening, EU sanctions checks, and the mandatory filing of the Luxembourg balance-of-payments statistical return for any transfer exceeding EUR 12,500. Non-EU remittances may require underlying commercial documentation and, for SCSp pass-through distributions, a certificate of tax residence to evidence beneficial ownership.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or repatriation requirement exists under Luxembourg or Eurosystem law. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency indefinitely and converted to EUR at market rates at the receipt bank. Mandatory conversion ratios are not applicable. Only statistical reporting (balance-of-payments basis) applies to outbound/inbound transactions above EUR 12,500.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passportable into Luxembourg under PSD2 can support basic EUR/USD euro-denominated collection and payment flows. However, most EMIs are reluctant to onboard partnership structures with multi-tier beneficial ownership, and none offer commercial letters of credit, trade finance, or physical custody. Offshore EMIs outside the EEA lack passporting rights and will be blocked by correspondent banks, making them unusable for material treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks mandate an in-person meeting for at least one authorized signatory (usually the general partner's managing director) at the bank's Luxembourg branch. Remote onboarding is accepted for low-risk EU resident signatories using a notarized power of attorney, live video identification, and certified passport/address copies. For non-EU resident directors of the SCSp, the systemic banks (BGL BNP Paribas, BIL) typically require physical presence. In all cases, the bank's risk committee will require explanation of the SCSp's operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex partnership structure with silent limited partners and a corporate general partner, creating potential opacity around ultimate beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full organizational chart; certified copy of the SCSp partnership agreement; notarized list of all partners with their respective capital commitments; ultimate beneficial ownership declarations on CSSF Form; notarized resolution from the general partner appointing the account signatories; negative news/media search report; written explanation of the SCSp's commercial purpose in food manufacturing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection from non-EU shareholders without documented source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder bank statements for 12 months; tax returns or audited accounts; asset disposal/sale agreements; business plan with cash flow forecasts; certificate of incorporation of the direct shareholder; declarations confirming the funds are free of criminal proceeds and directly tied to rice noodle plant equipment purchases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border procurement and trade flows with East Asian counterparties, raising sanctions and trade-based money laundering flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices and signed supply contracts for rice, seasoning and packaging; bills of lading and customs import/export declarations; inspection/product quality certificates; complete counterparty KYC packs; description of the physical supply chain and logistics route; relevant EU/exempted import licenses for food products.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived lack of economic substance in Luxembourg for an SCSp often associated with fund structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed lease for registered office and physical operations; employment contracts and payroll data for local sales, quality assurance and administrative staff; plant production schedules and delivery documentation; regulatory food manufacturing licenses; Luxembourg VAT and social security registrations; board meeting minutes evidencing local management decisions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For EUR capital contributions, use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with purpose code CAPT (capital transfer). For non-EUR inbound transfers, use SWIFT MT103 with instruction field 70 referencing the capital contribution agreement and the SCSp registration number (Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register). Prior to execution, the receiving bank will require the completed balance-of-payments declaration (codes EU12/CAP) for any amount above EUR 12,500. The bank will verify the remitter's identity against the KYC-approved partner list and may request the contribution resolution of the general partner. No CSSF or BCL pre-authorization is required, but the bank must be able to establish the source of funds through accompanying documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for raw materials (rice, tapioca starch, seasoning) and packaging are executed through: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct TT payments; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 for large recurring imports from East Asia; and (iii) documentary collection (D/P or D/A) for low-value transactions. All payments are initiated via the bank's corporate e-banking portal with dual-signature authorization. The bank will require the underlying invoice, purchase order, and, for LC issuance, at least 30% cash cover or an approved credit facility. Payments to high-risk third countries trigger enhanced due diligence, including an export license/end-use declaration where necessary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD forward contracts (up to 24 months) against USD-denominated equipment and packaging imports
EUR/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for settlement of supplies priced in RMB, as CNH is offshore and non-deliverable in the main Luxembourg dealing market
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) for short-term rollover of working capital balances
Plain-vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/VND options for targeted acquisition of seasoning and noodle-processing equipment from Vietnam
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) where bank financing is structured as a foreign-currency-backed mortgage or equipment loan

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and financial statements deposit at the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS), subject to the SCSp filing exemption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months of the financial year-end: approval of the annual accounts must occur within six months and deposit within one month of approval; for a 31 December year-end, filing is due no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing exposes the general partner to administrative fines, daily fines after formal notice by the RCS, publication of the default in the Official Electronic Collection, and a court-ordered strike-off after repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg income allocation return for the fiscally transparent SCSp (partnership tax information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg direct tax administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual calendar deadline announced by the tax administration, generally by 31 December of the year following the tax period for mandatory e-filing; provisional tax instalments remain due during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessments, late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, administrative penalties, and criminal fines for intentional failure; a tax default does not itself trigger commercial strike-off but the general partner remains jointly liable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual internal certification of the statutory partner register and beneficial ownership record; event-driven update of the RBE filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General partner's corporate file; event-driven filing with the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE / Luxembourg Business Registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each anniversary of incorporation, the general partner must perform an internal audit of the register; any transfer of limited-partner interests or UBO change must be filed with the RBE within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil nullity of unrecorded transfers against third parties, responsibility of the general partner for inaccurate registers, and administrative or criminal fines for RBE late filings; prolonged inaction can lead to judicial strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance of the food business establishment registration for instant rice-noodle manufacturing and annual internal compliance review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Veterinary and Food Administration (ALVA); internal compliance file for the annual review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous registration requirement; annual internal review on the anniversary of the registration and immediate notification of any changes in production conditions or sector classification (ISIC 1079)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or revocation of the food business approval, administrative fines and closure of the production line; strike-off is not applicable to this operational licence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a Luxembourg approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is required if the SCSp exceeds two of the three size tests: total balance-sheet assets above EUR 4,400,000, net turnover above EUR 8,800,000 and average workforce above 50 employees; below these thresholds the SCSp is exempt from a compulsory annual audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the law of 10 August 1915 and the law of 19 December 2019 on annual accounts, with optional consolidated IFRS reporting if the SCSp forms part of a group; tax-transparent treatment does not remove the bookkeeping and annual accounts drawing obligation

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg does not impose a separate annual UBO declaration: the SCSp must be in a continuously accurate RBE state. The general partner performs an annual anniversary certification of the partner register and beneficial-ownership analysis; any limited-partner interest transfer or direct or indirect shareholding change must be endorsed in the statutory register and reported to the RBE within 30 days. The annual certification is retained as corporate evidence and prevents the register of members from becoming outdated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of limited partners (members) with contributions and transfer history
Register of general partner and managers (equivalent of directors' register)
Minute book of partner resolutions and management decisions
Register of documentary evidence for RBE / UBO analysis

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,500 - 6,000 per annum for a Luxembourg registered agent, domiciliation service and corporate secretarial function for an SCSp
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 22,000 per annum when a full statutory audit is required; below audit thresholds, USD 0 and only agreed-upon procedures may be arranged

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline for Luxembourg City (national Corporate Income Tax 'IRC' 15% + solidarity surcharge 7% of IRC + Municipal Business Tax 'ICT' 6.75%). The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default: the rate is applied at partner level only, or at entity level if the SCSp validly elects to be taxed as a corporation. Non-resident partners are taxed only on the Luxembourg-source share attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment, subject to treaty allocation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividends and capital gains where the partner holds at least 10% of the share capital or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million (dividends) or EUR 6 million (capital gains), with a continuous 12-month holding period. IP regime: 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income under the OECD nexus ratio, producing an effective rate of approximately 4.98% on the national IRC component. Investment tax credits for digitalisation, energy transition and certain equipment up to 13.5% of qualifying investments. At transparent-partnership level, the SCSp benefits from pass-through treatment; municipal business tax may be assessed on the SCSp as the commercial operator while income tax is borne by the partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: unlimited (no statutory expiry under Article 114 LIR; loss carryback generally not permitted)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune); mandatory electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu Espace professionnel and the ACD (Administration des contributions directes) e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months of the close of the tax year (30 June N+1 for a 31 December year-end); the ACD routinely grants extension until 31 December N+1. Non-resident partners with a Luxembourg PE file on the same deadline for the Luxembourg-source share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification of the taxpayer; name, legal form, address, national register number (RCS Luxembourg).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For transparent SCSp, Box 1 identifies the SCSp and each direct partner with its full foreign tax identification number; the return is a declarative partner-reconciliation statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates (exercice social).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calendar-year alignment is presumed for foreign partners; deviations require explicit reconciliation with the foreign tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and profit and loss statement in accordance with Luxembourg GAAP; includes inventory of retort pouches and finished instant rice noodles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partner includes only the allocable profit share from the Luxembourg PE; the full financial statements must be attached to support the allocation key.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net result before tax adjustments; reconciliation of commercial accounting profit to taxable result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Partnership profit-sharing ratio must be evidenced by the SCSp partnership deed to determine the non-resident partner's taxable slice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible charges added back: fines, non-documented benefits in kind, excess interest expense, taxes paid abroad, and 50% of interest and financing costs for ICT add-back purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners add back their pro-rata share of non-deductible expenses; double-counting with the municipal business tax computation must be avoided.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible items: depreciation, salaries, social security contributions, third-party logistics, packaging raw materials and quality-certification expenses for the food plant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically connected to the Luxembourg PE are allocable to a non-resident partner; head-office overhead must be supported by cost-sharing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participating interests and financial income: dividend and capital-gain exclusions under the participation exemption; foreign withholding tax credits claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must exclude exempt income and attach a Tax Residence Certificate and holding-period evidence if treaty credit or exemption is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation and allocation of loss carryforwards against current-year profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards utilised by the transparent entity are allocated pro rata to partners; partner-level carryforwards are not offset in the SCSp return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: IRC 15%, solidarity surcharge 7%, and municipal business tax 6.75% (Luxembourg City rate); investment tax credits and IP box exemptions applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners compute Luxembourg CIT on the PE-attributable profit at the same 24.94% combined rate unless a treaty allocates the profit to the residence state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction annex: list of cross-border transactions with associated enterprises, transfer pricing method applied, and confirmation that Local File / Master File documentation exists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners transacting with the SCSp (e.g., procurement of rice, seasoning, packaging) must disclose the transactions and be prepared to submit a TP Local File on demand.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing coercive fine (astreinte) up to EUR 1,200 per return; automatic late-payment interest at 0.6% per month on assessed amounts; ex officio estimated assessment with loss of deduction claims; non-electronic filing may be rejected; wilful omission exposes criminal tax fraud sanctions (fine up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% final Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid by a Luxembourg corporation. For a pure transparent SCSp, profit distributions to partners are not treated as dividends and no Luxembourg withholding tax is levied; the 15% statutory rate binds only where the SCSp has elected opaque corporate taxation or where the distribution is disguised as a shareholder remuneration mechanism.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A partner invoking a double tax agreement (DTA) reduced rate must (i) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its residence state; (ii) file a relief-at-source application with the ACD before the distribution date, attaching the SCSp partnership deed, the holding-period and shareholding evidence, and a position paper on the transparent character of the SCSp; (iii) renew the application annually. Where 15% has already been withheld, the partner files a refund claim with the ACD within the statutory limitation period, supported by TRC, audited accounts and proof of tax residence; the ACD applies the mutual agreement procedure route where treaty interpretation conflict arises.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on interest payments (0%) and no withholding tax on royalties (0%). This zero-rate applies to debt interest, shareholder loans, license fees, trademarks, patents and know-how paid by an SCSp to non-resident recipients without any substantive withholding burden; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive and DTA restrictions are therefore administratively redundant for Luxembourg payers. Payments for toll manufacturing services, quality certification and logistics are classified as business profits/technical services, likewise free of Luxembourg WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where the aggregate annual value of related-party transactions exceeds EUR 1,000,000; Master File mandatory where the consolidated group turnover reaches EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting notification threshold at EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue; all thresholds stated in EUR (local currency of Luxembourg).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) for rice, packaging film and seasoning procurement; wholesale distribution of retort noodle products
Resale Price method for controlled distribution to group sales platforms and supermarket chains
Cost Plus method for contract manufacturing, toll blending and co-packing services
TNMM (Transaction Net Margin Method) as the most common LPs-based method for routine food-manufacturing and logistics functions, using EBIT/Net-Sales or Berry ratios
Profit Split method for integrated supply-chain arrangements involving unique intangibles, brand trademarks and shared R&D
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) does not apply in Luxembourg. Instead, Luxembourg enforces substance through (i) the ATAD GAAR and the abuse-of-law doctrine (gestaltungsmissbrauch), (ii) place-of-effective-management residency tests, (iii) the statutory nexus requirement for the IP exemption, and (iv) the 2018/2019 substance rules for tax ruling applicants. A manufacturing SCSp operating a retort noodle plant with staff, plant, equipment, inventory and business controls inherently satisfies substance; passive holding or invoice-centric SCSp arrangements remain at risk of recharacterisation and treaty-benefit denial.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.statutory_documentation_file_scope: The Local File must include entity structure chart, principal business functions, risks assumed, tangible and intangible assets, intercompany agreements, transfer pricing method selection, benchmarking study, and financial comparability analysis; penalties attach for non-production within the ACD's 30-day demand period.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Willful Fiscal Fraud (soustraction frauduleuse d'impôts)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Luxembourg PE income, fabrication of false purchase invoices for rice or packaging, concealment of bank accounts receiving SWIFT LC proceeds, or fictitious partner profit allocations diverting taxable profit to non-resident shell partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years; administrative surcharges of 10%-20% on the evaded tax, late-payment interest at 0.6% per month, confiscation of the proceeds, and loss of all deduction and exemption claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and gérants are personally liable for the evaded tax where they ordered or tolerated the concealment; criminal conviction triggers civil restitution, removal from management, passport surrender and travel bans pending proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or produce the Local File / Master File within 30 days after the ACD's demand where related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000; pricing of rice-noodle intercompany sales, royalties or management fees outside the arm's length range without benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward adjustment of taxable profit to arm's length level, reclassification of excessive payments as non-deductible or constructive dividends, 0.6% monthly late interest, coercive fines up to EUR 1,200, and, in intentional cases, criminal tax fraud prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign intercompany agreements knowingly below arm's length expose themselves to joint liability for the corporate tax shortfall under the extended-liability doctrine; they may be barred from managing a Luxembourg entity following a fraud conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Law / Artificial Shell Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing an SCSp without operational substance solely to exploit tax transparency and the DTA network, with no genuine business activity, no premises, no employees and no commercial risk in the instant noodle manufacturing chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the arrangement, denial of pass-through status, imposition of the 15% dividend withholding tax on remittances, retroactive assessment against the partners, 10% abuse-of-law surcharge, and mandatory disclosure penalties under DAC6 up to EUR 250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who established the sham SCSp may be personally assessed for the unpaid corporate taxes and interest; criminal courts may also impose custodial sentences and travel restrictions where the sham facilitated large-scale cross-border tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Trade-Based Money Laundering via Swift LC / TT Wire Trade Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Over- or under-invoicing of rice noodle export consignments, circular trade transactions with shell counterparties, cash prepayments above the EUR 10,000 cash threshold, false commodity descriptions on bills of lading, or use of payment intermediaries without beneficial-owner identification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 5,000,000 for legal persons and imprisonment up to five years for natural persons under the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004 (as amended); confiscation of the funds, freezing of the LC proceeds, and professional debarment of the compliance officer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve suspicious LC/TT transactions without adequate KYC and sanctions screening are personally liable for AML fines and civil damages; in aggravated cases the courts impose exit bans, freeze personal assets and issue international arrest warrants.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Director Personal Liability and Veil-Piercing for Corporate Tax Debts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Gross mismanagement of the SCSp leading to insolvency with outstanding tax liabilities; concealment of assets; failure to maintain books and records; distribution of capital while taxes remain unpaid; fraudulent transfer pricing that hollows out the Luxembourg entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Action en comblement de passif: directors must make good the company's deficit where a faute grave et caractérisée caused the insolvency; bankruptcy ban prohibiting management of a Luxembourg company up to 10 years; civil fines and restitution orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal bank accounts and assets of directors can be attached; the ACD may obtain a travel ban (interdiction de sortie du territoire) pending criminal proceedings; imprisonment up to five years applies for abuse of corporate assets or fraudulent misrepresentation of the SCSp's tax position.
